subject: Re: SprintX — sudden token throughput suppression & p99 spike
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@sprintx.ai>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, SLA Ops <ops@sprintx.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Token throughput drop + p99 spikes since 11/18 deploy

Rafael/team,

We're seeing a hard regression that started ~22:00 UTC on 2026-11-18 after the model-serving changes. Key observations from our dashboards: p95 latency jumped from ~120ms -> ~420ms and p99 from ~300ms -> ~1.2s for our hosted endpoints. Token/sec (measured as tokens generated / sec of generation) fell from ~9k -> ~1.6k on our normal 512-seq workloads. Error rate is slightly elevated (0.5% -> 1.7%) but the main pain is throughput/latency.

This is high impact for our real-time chat use case — bursts are timing out downstream and page-level SLA alerts are firing. The timing lines up with a platform rollout noted in our onboarding notes: "kernel selector + new q4_1 quant profile enabled" around 22:00 UTC. I attached a small profiling dump and the traces we pulled from the client-side.

Attachments: sprintx_qprofile_20261119.csv, p99_traces_20261119.png

Can we get urgent triage and either a temporary rollback/fallback? We are escalating internally and may need exec attention if this is not resolved quickly.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Head of AI Ops, SprintX
alex.chen@sprintx.ai

Subject: Re: Token throughput drop + p99 spikes since 11/18 deploy

Quick findings from initial logs and traces:
- The runtime's kernel-autoselect heuristic routed SprintX traffic to packed-gemm-q4 for many of their short-sequence requests (mean seq len ~40). On our testbeds, packed-gemm-q4 shows better token/sec at very long sequences (>=1024) but underutilizes GPU parallelism for short sequences, which can drop T/sec by ~60–75% in some configs.
- The q4_1 quant profile introduces a slightly denser cache layout which increases KV cache pressure and exacerbates the packed-gemm path's inefficiencies for multi-tenant pools.

Immediate TTL mitigation: force kernel override to baseline-fp16 for SprintX. Commands (ops):
- set customer_override kernel=baseline-fp16 --customer SprintX --policy canary=10%
- monitor p95/p99 and token/sec for 10–30 minutes

Expected impact: p95 should drop back toward pre-change values (120–200ms) and tokens/sec should recover toward ~8–9k for the canary. If good, expand to 100% and follow with a controlled quant-profile rollback or kernel-selector heuristic tweak.

I'll prepare a quick bench harness to compare packed-gemm-q4 vs baseline-fp16 on their trace corpus; ETA 90 minutes.

— Aditya Rao
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Subject: SprintX incident — summary & next steps

Alex / SprintX ops — summary from our side and next steps: 

What happened (summary):
- Kernel selector rolled change on 2026-11-18 22:00 UTC which allowed packed-gemm-q4 to be selected for many short-sequence requests. In combination with q4_1 quant profile rollout this produced lower GPU parallelism for the most common sequence lengths and increased KV cache pressure, resulting in a ~60% drop in tokens/sec and p95/p99 regressions.

Immediate actions taken:
- 2026-11-19 11:02 PST: applied kernel override to baseline-fp16 (canary -> 10%).
- 2026-11-19 11:10 PST: expanded override to 100% after validation.
- 2026-11-19 11:30 PST: moved customer to dedicated-ephemeral-3 pool while we stabilize.

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Short term (Aditya / 24–48h): run bench harness and update kernel-selector heuristics to avoid packed-gemm-q4 for seq-len < 256 or when quant-profile q4_1 is active.
- Mid term (Serving + Runtime / 1 week): add quant-profile safety gate to rollout (per-customer sequencing) + improve canary metrics for tokens/sec.
- Customer remediation (Vanessa / Sales Ops / 48–72h): formal credit proposal and SLA remediation note.
- Postmortem & Tech writeup (Markus / Aditya / 5 business days): incident writeup with repro, perf curves, and recommended guardrails.

Attachments: sprintx_qprofile_20261119.csv, kernel_switch_log_20261119.txt, p99_traces_20261119.png

We'll host the postmortem call tomorrow 10:00 PST — calendar invite sent to this thread. Thanks again for the quick confirmation and patience, Alex. We'll share the full artifact bundle in SUP-3219 and the Drive link.

— Rafael Mendes
